about: The epistola of the formulary “Low Sunday” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: Beloved: Everyone who has been born of God overcomes the world. And this is the victory that overcomes the world: our faith. Who overcomes the world but the one who believes that Jesus is the Son of God? This is the One who came through water and blood, Jesus Christ: not in water alone, but in water and blood. And the Spirit bears witness, because Christ is the truth. For there are three who bear witness in heaven: the Father, the Word, and the Holy Spirit. And these three are one. And there are three who bear witness on earth: the Spirit, water, and blood; and these three are one. If we accept human testimony, God’s testimony is greater, because this is God’s testimony, which is greater: for He has testified about His Son. Whoever believes in the Son of God has God’s testimony within themselves.

ex.w056: Quoniam can introduce the reason here: the Spirit bears witness because Christ is the truth. It can also introduce the content of the witness: the Spirit bears witness that Christ is the truth. In both readings, Christ remains the subject of “is the truth”.
ex.w112: Quoniam links these words to the preceding statement about God’s testimony. It can introduce a reason (“because He has testified about His Son”) or explain the content of that testimony (“that He has testified about His Son”).
